audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty prose was generic scaler-boilerplate and the full-layer level chart said 'Skill' for levels 1-5 and level-first-item while the content layer said Karma/Karma/Karma/Karma/Skill/Azir. The page rendered two different answers to who wins each stage.
audit.why: Azir has no Sand Soldier until he puts a point in W and Conquering Sands is 740 range against Karma's 950 Inner Flame, so the early lane is genuinely Karma's, not a coinflip. After his first item the soldier line outranges her and the lane is his.
audit.corrected: Full-layer phases[0..3].side moved to Karma and phases[5].side moved to Azir, matching the content layer and the packet levelChart, with each why rewritten to match the new verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike prose named no real cooldowns and the level-6 row claimed Karma gains nothing while ignoring that Azir gains Emperor's Divide.
audit.why: Karma's level 6 is only a Mantra rank; Azir's is a 120/105/90s wall that cancels her commit outright. That is the real shape of the spike trade.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states the 120s Emperor's Divide against Karma's non-ult 6; phases[5].why states his first item pushing soldier range past her 950 Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and described Shifting Sands only as 'his shield-dash to a soldier'.
audit.why: Shifting Sands is 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s and is Azir's only escape; Emperor's Divide is 120/105/90s. Those two numbers are the entire green-light system in this lane. Karma's W (Focused Resolve) roots and reveals, and her R is 40/38/36/34s.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t now carry the real 22s-to-16s Shifting Sands number and the 120s Emperor's Divide.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flagged wants.foe[2] 'Land Emperor's Divide' as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: Emperor's Divide is the correct Riot name for Azir's R per the kit file. This is a suspectNames false positive; no edit made.

edits.before: Q-poke wins level 1 against nearly everyone — the lane starts as your spam war; respect only mana.
edits.after: Azir has no Sand Soldier until he ranks W, so Inner Flame poke is free — your only limit here is mana.

edits.before: Mantra online from level 1 means RQ is already a third of a health bar — spend it on real windows, not waves.
edits.after: Mantra is up from level 1: RQ chunks him before soldiers matter — spend it when he steps to last-hit, not on the wave.

edits.before: Full kit: W tether roots overstayers and E speeds every trade exit. Your early is the best in the utility class.
edits.after: Soul Shield speeds your exit and Focused Resolve roots him if he steps up; Shifting Sands is a 22s escape at rank 1.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — the RQ chunk cycles every 30 seconds. Chip him below half and hold the kill window.
edits.after: Lost Chapter timing — RQ cycles fast while Conquering Sands still costs him 110 mana. Chip him and hold the window.

edits.before: No new ult — your 6 is a Mantra rank: faster cycles, bigger RQs. Press the early lead before scaling lanes wake up.
edits.after: You get no new ult; he gets Emperor's Divide on 120s, which walls off your commit outright. Even trade of spikes.

edits.before: Blackfire/Luden's spike: RQ-W chains threaten kills outright. The lane is now or never — you fall off politely.
edits.after: His first item pushes the soldier line past your 950 Q — he farms you from safety and your kill window has closed.

edits.before: Late Karma is a utility engine: RE shields the team, W roots the diver, and RQ pokes the objective setup.
edits.after: His soldiers hit from screen range and Emperor's Divide splits your team — you shrink to shielding and peel.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Azir wins by reaching items, then poking with soldier lines from beyond your Q while Emperor's Divide covers him.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your RE shield-speed has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1 and 16s at rank 5 — his only escape. Once he dashes to a soldier, that whole window is yours to W-root and RQ him. - Emperor's Divide is 120s at rank 1: if he spends it to peel himself, your next commit is free. Count both.

edits.before: If Azir takes first blood, tighten up: Shifting Sands is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q and stay relevant through shields and roots.
edits.after: If Azir takes first blood he reaches his item spike early and your one window shuts. Farm with Q at max range, never contest a wave his soldiers already cover, and stay relevant by shielding and rooting for your jungler.

edits.before: Carry early or enable late — RQ chips win lanes; RE + roots win the teamfights your early lead bought.
edits.after: Carry before his first item — RQ chips him off the wave; after it, RE and roots keep your carries alive.

edits.before: Ahead, sprint: RQ Azir off every wave, take plates with the lead, and W-root river picks — Karma leads are sprints, not marathons.
edits.after: Ahead, sprint: RQ him off the wave every cycle, take plates before his first item, and W-root him whenever Shifting Sands is on its 22s.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, and on real windows RQ-W: the chunk plus tether-root turns a poke trade into a kill setup — E out before the answer.
edits.after: Inner Flame reaches 950; Conquering Sands only 740. Stand at your range and poke him every time he walks up to farm.

edits.before: Azir whiffs Shifting Sands and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: His first item flips the lane — bank plates while it is still yours.

edits.before: That is Azir’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Even farm is his win — he passes you at items, so build the lead now.

edits.before: Your tether breaks if YOU walk away — holding the root means holding your ground for two seconds you must plan for.
edits.after: Mantra spent on a wave is the RQ that would have chunked him at 740 range the moment he stepped up to soldier-farm.

edits.before: Spending Mantra on wave-clear while behind on poke — Karma without RQ banked is a support who took mid's farm.
edits.after: Post-item his soldiers outrange your 950 Q — walking up to poke means eating soldier lines for one Inner Flame.

edits.before: Track Azir’s Shifting Sands: His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Shifting Sands: a 22s-to-16s shield-dash onto one of his soldiers, and his only escape. While it is down, W-root and RQ him freely.

edits.before: Karma's all-in burst still outpaces Azir's ramping soldier damage.
edits.after: Your RQ chunk still outpaces his ramping Sand Soldier damage.

edits.before: Both ultimates are equally game-changing here, making it a true coinflip.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide on 120s answers your commit; Mantra answers his.
